## Exam Scenario

The data read in below consists of a sample of 386 African-American patients. The data was collected to research the relationship among a number of predictor variables and whether the patient had been diagnosed with diabetes or not.  Among the possible predictors are:
chol (cholesterol), stab.glu (stabilized glucose), hdl (hdl cholesterol), ratio (chol/hdl), glyhb(glycosolated hemoglopin - a measure of the amount of sugar in the blood), bp.1s (first systolic blood pressure), bp.1d (first diastolic blood pressure), hip (hip measurement), and time.ppn (number of minutes after eating, when blood was taken).  We will 
consider the analysis of whether people are diagnosed with diabetes or not in this problem.  

For this exam we will **NOT** be using the variable glyhb because it is essentially used to diagnose diabetes.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
#dia.data <- read.csv("data/diabetes.csv")
```
:::


1.  [20 points] Using exploratory data analysis, decide which variables might be appropriate to include when modeling the diabetes variable (ignore glyhb).  Explain how you came to your conclusion referring to your output.

2.  [20 points] Find the best 1-variable model for diabetes.  Explain why you think yours is the best.

3.  [25 points]  Find the best multivariable model for diabetes.  Again, explain why you think this is the best multivariable model.

4.  [10 points] Use appropriate inference to compare your models from questions 2 and 3.  Which of the two models would you ultimately use and why?
